note: Set B reproduces the table rows it cites with correct values, units and column bindings (TwGJStif 472.75E+9 and 89.13E+9, TwFAIner/TwSSIner, TwFAcgOf, TwSSStif), whereas Set A invents or misbinds several entries (TwGJStiff 134.15 and TwFAlSef 62.66 taken from the TwEAStif column, a fabricated TwFAlSef 218.3E+3 N/m, TMassDen 556.8, TwFASStiff 614.5) and drops the E+9 exponent on several stiffness values. Set A also mislabels the 38.234 m mass-center value as tower height 28.34 m, while Set B makes the same height error but keeps the mass-center claim correct. Set B's main faults are a few digit slips (556.87, 614.85E+9, 347 kg) and a garbled column label (TWasSif), plus the same duplicated rows as A.
remarks: Both sets miss the key material and geometry facts in the prose: base diameter 6 m, top diameter 3.87 m, top thickness 0.019 m, Young's modulus 210 GPa, shear modulus 80.8 GPa, effective density 8,500 kg/m3 (vs 7,850 kg/m3 typical), linear taper assumption, and the 30% thickness increase. Both also duplicate the same table rows (TwGJStif 472.75E+9, TwSSStif 614.34E+9, integrated mass) and both bind the 38.234 m mass-center value to 'height' in one claim. Several Set A quotes (e.g. 'TwFAlSef 218.3E+3 (N/m)', 'TwGJStiff 134.15E+9') do not appear anywhere on the page and look fabricated; column names in both sets are garbled (TwFAlNer, TwFASStiff, TwSccOg, TWasSif).
